original_title: Subcellular spatiotemporal proteomics delineates distinct phases of ER stress proteostatic response
title: Tracking the ER's stress response protein by protein, over time
blurb: A spatiotemporal proteomics method, SPLAT-TR, follows synthesis, degradation and localization for over 4,000 proteins through early and prolonged ER stress, splitting the proteostatic response into distinct phases instead of one averaged snapshot. More valuable as a dataset other people can mine than as a single finding.

original_title: Transfer Hydrogenation of Nitrones to Hydroxylamine Derivatives with PhSiH3
title: PhSiH3 turns nitrones into hydroxylamines, no metal required
blurb: A metal- and additive-free transfer hydrogenation that converts both ketone- and aldehyde-derived nitrones into hydroxylamines in good to excellent yield under mild conditions, scalable and tolerant of bromo, chloro, fluoro, CF3, thioether, thiophene and furan groups. Unglamorous mechanism, but one less metal to strip out of the product afterward.

original_title: Duplex Paternò–Büchi Isobaric Reagents for One-Step C═C-Resolved Lipid Isomer Quantification
title: Telling apart lipid double-bond isomers without a separate ID step
blurb: Duplex Paternò-Büchi tags (AMPE-tags) derivatize the C=C bond, pin down its exact position, and hand you relative quant, all in one reaction, for isomers that share the same mass and sum composition and would otherwise be invisible to standard lipidomics.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: (Hetero)Adamantane Synthesis: A Triple Alkylation Reaction
title: A shortcut into the adamantane cage, three alkylations at a time
blurb: A convergent triple-alkylation route assembles (hetero)adamantanes with carbon, silicon, or germanium at the bridgeheads in one go, aimed at giving surface and materials chemists an easier way into a scaffold that's normally a slog to build with interchangeable functional groups.

original_title: Chemical Design Rule for Ultraviolet-Emitting Color Centers: The Role of Host Ionicity
title: What actually sets the color of a UV color center: ionicity, not the bandgap
blurb: Zero-phonon line energy in UV single-photon emitters tracks the host's bonding character, covalent versus ionic, via the bonding-antibonding splitting of the defect states, not just how wide the bandgap is. Diamond's covalent divacancy is the test case, turning into a design rule for picking better UV-emitter hosts instead of just scanning bandgaps.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Multistate reactivity of weak-field clusters at ambient temperatures
title: Some clusters are reacting through excited states you'd never guess were populated
blurb: In polynuclear clusters, coupling between local high-spin centers can leave excited states low enough to be thermally populated at room temperature, opening reaction pathways the usual ground-state-only picture misses. Sorting out the mechanism of that is apparently the whole problem.

original_title: A 3D Cycloparaphenylene‐Cored Trimeric Electron Acceptor Regulates Acceptor Fibril Morphology for 20.6%‐Efficient Ternary Organic Solar Cells
title: A curved, 3D electron acceptor gets ternary solar cells to 20.6%
blurb: CPP-3Y bolts a cycloparaphenylene nanohoop onto Y-series acceptors, giving a radially conjugated, curved, low-crystallinity acceptor instead of the usual flat one. As a third component it reshapes acceptor fibril morphology and pushes the ternary cell to 20.6% efficiency, a rare case of 3D macrocycle topology actually paying off in device numbers.

original_title: Deoxyfluorination of Aliphatic Alcohols by PyFluor/DBU: Mechanism, Reactivity, and Substrate Selectivity
title: Why PyFluor/DBU fluorinates some alcohols and stalls on others
blurb: A mechanistic dig, theory plus experiment, into deoxyfluorination with PyFluor/DBU, mapping the competing side reactions that make certain aliphatic alcohols reluctant to fluorinate. More a substrate-selectivity explanation than a new reagent, but useful for knowing when a sluggish substrate isn't worth fighting.

original_title: Finding the Right TEMPO: Multi-Objective Virtual Screening and Experimental Validation of TEMPO Derivatives for Aqueous Redox Flow Battery Catholytes
title: Screening 182 TEMPOs to find one that won't degrade in your flow battery
blurb: A multi-objective virtual screen balancing redox potential, stability, and synthetic accessibility across 182 TEMPO derivatives for aqueous flow battery catholytes flags two unexplored candidates, MC-TEMPO and DEA-TEMPO. Redox potential and predicted degradation resistance only correlate moderately, so picking on voltage alone would miss the more stable options.

original_title: Ru Single-Atom-Nanoparticle Synergy Induces Interfacial Electron Redistribution for Complete Selectivity Reversal in CO2 Hydrogenation
title: Same Ru catalyst, two products, just by changing single atom vs. nanoparticle
blurb: Ru nanoparticles on TiO2 run the reverse water-gas shift and spit out CO, but add single Ru atoms at the nanoparticle interface and selectivity flips to about 100% methane between 250 and 400°C. In-situ spectroscopy plus DFT trace the flip to a temperature-dependent dual pathway, a full selectivity reversal from an interfacial electron effect rather than a new metal.

original_title: Rongalite-Promoted One-Pot Reductive Cyclization Strategy for the Construction of Pyrrolo[1,2-α]quinoxalines from 1-(2-Nitrophenyl)pyrroles
title: Rongalite does double duty building quinoxaline-fused pyrroles
blurb: A transition-metal-free route to pyrrolo[1,2-a]quinoxalines where rongalite both reduces the nitro group and supplies the one-carbon unit that closes the ring, all in one pot. Radical-scavenger and formaldehyde-detection control experiments back up that dual role rather than just asserting it.

original_title: Water-Steam-Assisted Synthesis of Imine-Linked COF-432 for Atmospheric Water Harvesting
title: Steam instead of solvent to grow a water-harvesting COF
blurb: COF-432, an imine-linked framework for pulling water out of air, comes out crystalline via steam-assisted synthesis instead of the usual solvent-heavy solvothermal cook. Dialing in steam source, acetic acid dosage, temperature, and time gets it there, a greener route to the same material rather than a new one.

original_title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan (DS-8201a) Versus Investigator's Choice for HER2-low Breast Cancer That Has Spread or Cannot be Surgically Removed [DESTINY-Breast04]
title: T-DXd faces off against chemo in HER2-low breast cancer
blurb: Phase 3 trial from Daiichi Sankyo pitting trastuzumab deruxtecan against the oncologist's choice of chemo, capecitabine included, in breast cancer that's metastasized or can't be resected. The HER2-low part is the interesting bit, since that's a population that historically got waved off HER2-targeted therapy entirely. Trial's completed, so results should be out there to chase down.

original_title: Sodium borohydride: repurposing from a reducing agent to a reductive cyclization reagent for N -(2-iodoaryl)acrylamides
title: NaBH4 moonlights as a cyclization reagent
blurb: Sodium borohydride, normally just the reducing agent you grab off the shelf, turns out to drive a reductive cyclization of N-(2-iodoaryl)acrylamides straight to oxindoles, no external initiator required. One less reagent cluttering the pot.

original_title: From Peripheral Ag Sites to an Ag-Based Framework: Regulating CO2 Electroreduction Selectivity and Stability in V–Ag Nanoclusters
title: Same metals, different scaffold, different CO2 chemistry
blurb: Two atomically precise V-Ag nanoclusters built from the same components come out with different architectures, one with peripheral Ag+ sites perched on a polyoxovanadate scaffold, the other with an integrated Ag-based framework. That architecture alone shifts both CO2 electroreduction selectivity and how long the catalyst holds up, a cleaner structure-property link than these nanocluster papers usually manage.

original_title: Safety Hazard of the Thermal Decomposition of Difluoromethyl and -Methoxy Arenes Catalyzed by Boron Derivatives
title: Your difluoromethoxy boronic acid might not like being warm
blurb: Prompted by actual lab incidents, a DSC study found that aryl boronic acids or boronate esters carrying a difluoromethoxy or difluoromethyl group decompose exothermically at surprisingly low temperatures, both on their own and when just sitting next to other otherwise-stable compounds. Gets worse the closer the two groups are sterically. Worth running a DSC before you scale that reaction.

original_title: CCSBase2: A Unified Benchmark Dataset and Machine Learning Framework for Robust CCS Prediction
title: A benchmark to keep CCS prediction models honest
blurb: Collision cross section is supposed to help identify unknown analytes in ion mobility-MS, but measured values are sparse and current ML predictors don't generalize well outside their training set's chemical space. CCSBase2 is a unified benchmark dataset and framework meant to actually test that generalizability instead of letting models grade their own homework.

original_title: Concise Route to a Fully Tetrazolyl-Substituted Imidazole Isomer for Connectivity-Guided Energetic Material Design
title: Same energetic imidazole, three routes, not all equal
blurb: A new fully tetrazolyl-substituted imidazole, 2,4,5-tris(1H-tetrazol-5-yl)-1H-imidazole, made concisely from a tricyanoimidazole precursor, gets lined up against two previously reported isomers with identical tetrazolyl composition. Same formula, same energetic groups, but the step count to get there differs, which is the actual finding: connectivity decides the synthesis burden, not just what atoms you end up with.

original_title: Cross-section measurement of (165)Ho(d,x) reactions and comparison of deuteron and proton activation of holmium for(165)Er production.
title: Deuterons vs protons for making Erbium-165
blurb: New cross-section measurements for holmium-165 hit with deuterons, set against proton activation, both routes eyed for producing Erbium-165. Not much more to it than the numbers, but that's exactly what isotope production planning runs on.

original_title: Multiplexed hormone immunoassays for women's health on a regenerable silicon photonic chip
title: A reusable chip that reads several hormones at once
blurb: Longitudinal hormone tracking has been stuck behind assays that are expensive, inconvenient, and can't multiplex, part of why hormone-informed care is such a neglected corner of women's health. This is the first demonstration of multiplexed hormone immunoassays on a silicon photonic chip that regenerates for reuse, aimed at routine longitudinal testing instead of one-off blood draws.

original_title: Chemodivergent Synthesis of Fused Indole and Spirocyclic Indoline Through Solo‐Coordination‐Vacant Ir(III) Pincer Complex‐Catalyzed Acylnitrenoid Transfer
title: One catalyst, one intermediate, two different indole scaffolds
blurb: A coordination-vacant Ir(III) pincer catalyst takes indole-derived dioxazolones through a shared iridium-nitrenoid intermediate, then routes it to either a fused indole or a spirocyclic indoline just by tweaking the conditions, branching via a 1,2-alkyl migration or a hydride transfer. Same starting material, same catalyst, the outcome decided after the fact.

original_title: Hydrogen Bonds Regulate Paramagnetic Spin Delocalization in Ferric Hemes
title: Hydrogen bonds as a dial for where the iron's spin goes
blurb: Using five-coordinate Fe(III) porphyrin complexes with systematically varied hydrogen bonding, this pairs experiment with theory to show H-bonds give a tunable route for spin delocalization out of the paramagnetic iron center and into the secondary coordination sphere. That kind of control has been seen in protein active sites before, but not engineered on demand in a synthetic system.

original_title: Argon Coordination to the 3d Transition-Metal Monohalides: A Systematic Study of σ-Acceptor Accessibility in Ar–MX (M = Sc–Cu; X = F, Cl, Br)
title: Argon will bond to a metal if you pick the right one
blurb: A systematic sweep of Ar coordination across the 3d monohalides, Sc through Cu with F, Cl, and Br, using DFT, EDA, and multireference calculations. The binding strength doesn't creep steadily across the row, it swings, tracking how much sigma-acceptor room is left on the metal for argon's 3p electrons to donate into. Argon is still argon, this is just finding the handful of cases where it's willing to shake hands.

original_title: Playing Domino with Carbon: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Methanol with Cobalt Phthalocyanine
title: Cobalt phthalocyanine keeps CO2 reduction going all the way to methanol
blurb: Most molecular CO2 electrocatalysts stop at CO or formate. CoPc's square-planar Co-N4 site apparently pushes through the full six-electron, six-proton chain to methanol via a cascade of proton-coupled electron transfers, one catalyst doing what usually takes a relay of them. The hard part was never getting electrons onto CO2, it's stopping hydrogen evolution and CO from winning along the way.

original_title: Ampere‐Level CO 2 ‐to‐Formate Electrosynthesis Over Grain‐Boundary‐Rich Sulfur‐Doped SnO 2 in Alkaline–Neutral–Acidic Electrolytes
title: Sulfur-doped SnO2 makes formate at amp-level current, and doesn't care what electrolyte you feed it
blurb: Sn catalysts for CO2-to-formate usually lose selectivity once you push the current density up, and acidic electrolytes make it worse. Loading the SnO2 with grain boundaries and sulfur dopants reportedly keeps formate selectivity at ampere-level currents across alkaline, neutral, and acidic media alike. The acidic-media part is the one worth watching, since that's where these catalysts usually fall apart.

original_title: Linker-Dependent Conformational Switching in Side-Chain-Type Ferrocene-Functionalized Nanohoops
title: Tether length decides whether ferrocene hides inside its own nanohoop or someone else's
blurb: Two ferrocene-tethered nanohoops differing only in linker length end up with different host-guest habits: the longer tether lets ferrocene tuck into its own ring as well as a neighbor's, the medium one only does the intermolecular version. DFT puts the rotational barrier for the tethered phenyl at a mild ~23 kcal/mol, so the ferrocene can spin a full 360 degrees inward under ordinary conditions. A tidy case of a couple extra methylenes rewriting the whole binding behavior.

original_title: Direct Observation of a Hydrogen‐Bonding Assisted Quasi‐Reversible Superoxo/Peroxo Interconversion in a Heme Model
title: Watching a heme model swap between superoxo and peroxo, mid-reaction, with cyclic voltammetry
blurb: Second-sphere urea groups on an iron-porphyrin build a hydrogen-bond network around a trapped water molecule, and that network stabilizes the Fe(III)-O2 superoxo state enough to catch it interconverting with the peroxo form quasi-reversibly on ordinary CV, no exotic spectroscopy required. First direct look at that redox couple behaving this way in a heme mimic, which matters for anyone modeling how O2 actually gets handled at these metal centers.

original_title: Mechanistic insights into potassium ion promotion of formate selectivity on copper clusters during carbon dioxide electroreduction
title: Potassium ions are quietly steering copper nanoclusters toward formate
blurb: Cation effects on CO2 reduction are well known for bulk copper electrodes, but nobody had isolated what K+ specifically does at copper nanoclusters until this quantum chemical model. The ion makes CO2 adsorption more exoergic, nudging the cluster's product mix toward formate. A mechanistic result for now, from simulation rather than a working electrode.

original_title: Pinacol boronates vanishing on silica
title: Pinacol boronates vanishing on silica
blurb: Grad student here, working on borylated bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes. My substrates all carry a Bpin on a secondary sp³ carbon, and I am losing catastrophic amounts of material on every column. I've quantified it and I'd like a sanity check plus ideas. The system. Crossed [2+2] photocycloaddition of an alkenyl-Bpin diene (ITX sensitizer, 395 nm, MeCN). The reaction is clean — crude NMR/GC shows only ITX, unreacted diene and product. Conversion is typically 30–50%, so I have to separate substrate from product. 1100 mg loaded, 51% conversion, long slow column, ~400 g silica (difficult separation). Tota

original_title: Diazonium coupling
title: Diazonium coupling
blurb: https://preview.redd.it/5hhgcetecash1.png?width=873&format=png&auto=webp&s=97d21a39c2259e1dffc9e209303ea900f2858690 I'm working on the coupling of a diazonium salt to salicylic acid. I have tried several conditions using different solvents (e.g., water, EtOH, ACN) in both acidic and basic conditions. Only got a trace of the desired product (3%) when using aqueous NaOH solution as the solvent. The diazonium salt is poorly soluble in water. I wonder if anyone has experience with a similar reaction and can suggest conditions I might try. Thanks.

original_title: Why ADC development needs new level of bioconjugation expertise - The Pharma Letter
title: Trade press discovers ADCs are hard to conjugate
blurb: A headline announcing that bioconjugation expertise matters for ADC development, with nothing under the hood. File under things everyone in the field already knew.

original_title: C‐Terminal Functionalization Methods of Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
title: The C-terminus finally gets its own review
blurb: 150 years of peptide chemistry and everyone kept modifying the N-terminus or the usual reactive side chains, lysine, cysteine, tyrosine, while the C-terminus stayed an afterthought. This review rounds up how to actually hit it selectively: classical coupling reagents, enzymatic tricks, and photo- or electrochemical decarboxylation.

original_title: STAT+: AstraZeneca invests $2 billion in Summit Therapeutics
title: AstraZeneca puts $2 billion behind Summit's bispecific
blurb: AstraZeneca is pairing Summit's PD-1/VEGF bispecific ivonescimab with its own antibody-drug conjugates. Big check for a combo that's still a bet on whether hitting two pathways at once beats an ADC running solo.

original_title: Phase II Study of 177Lu-DOTATATE Radionuclide in Adults With Progressive or High-risk Meningioma
title: Lutathera takes a shot at meningioma
blurb: NYU Langone's Phase II of 177Lu-DOTATATE in adults with progressive or high-risk meningioma is active but closed to new enrollment. No results yet, just a trial still running its course.

original_title: A multiscale quantitative systems pharmacology platform for early screening of MMAE-based antibody-drug conjugates
title: A QSP model tries to predict ADC behavior before you build one
blurb: A multiscale quantitative systems pharmacology model chaining systemic PK, single-cell disposition, and tumor distribution to predict how much unconjugated MMAE actually shows up inside a tumor. The pitch is using it early in discovery instead of after you've already made the conjugate, which is the part most QSP tools skip.

original_title: Webinar: From Facility to Delivery: Solving the Complex Science of ADC Linker-Payload Synthesis - BioSpace
title: A webinar on the ADC linker-payload headache
blurb: A BioSpace webinar walking through linker-payload synthesis from facility to delivery. No data here, just the pitch that it's complicated, which anyone who's made an ADC already knew.

original_title: Preclinical validation of AMPDA-HB derivatives integrating Hsp70-specific TPP motif and anti-CD2 single domain antibody radiolabeled by Al18F approach for PET tumor imaging
title: An Al-18F tracer aimed at Hsp70 via a nanobody
blurb: Two bifunctional versions of the AMPDA-HB chelator, built to carry the mild-conditions [Al18F]2+ label, get bolted onto a heat-shock-protein-70-targeting TPP motif and an anti-CD2 nanobody for PET tumor imaging. Preclinical validation only, so it's a proof that the chelator plays nice with a nanobody before anyone images a patient with it.
venue: European Journal of Medicinal Chemistry Reports

original_title: Integrated electrophysiological and payload-release assessment of neuronal responses to antibody-drug conjugates in human iPSC-derived sensory neurons: implications for in vitro neurotoxicity evaluation
title: Watching ADCs misbehave in a dish of human sensory neurons
blurb: Peripheral neuropathy from ADCs shows up even when the target antigen isn't on the neuron, and nobody's nailed down why. This platform pairs microelectrode array recordings of iPSC-derived sensory neurons with direct measurement of payload release, tying the electrophysiology to how much drug is actually escaping the conjugate. In vitro only, but it's the kind of assay that could catch neurotoxicity before it shows up in a trial.

original_title: Progress and challenges in traceless ligand-directed labelling chemistry
title: Labelling proteins and then letting the ligand walk away
blurb: Traceless ligand-directed labelling uses a binding ligand to steer a reactive group onto a nearby residue, then lets the ligand itself dissociate, leaving just the label. This review covers where the transfer and catalyst-tethered versions of the chemistry stand and what's actually new in the mechanism and scope.

original_title: Integrative structural modelling reveals the human Mic60-Mic19 subcomplex as a diffusion barrier in mitochondria
title: Structural evidence for the MICOS complex as a literal gate
blurb: Mic60-Mic19 was suspected to span mitochondrial crista junctions and act as a diffusion barrier, but the mechanism was unclear. A crystal structure of the N-terminal dimeric helical bundle of human Mic60, combined with prior structural and biochemical data, builds an integrative model of how the subcomplex's architecture actually does the gatekeeping.

original_title: Preclinical Evaluation and Preliminary Clinical Study of Al18F-NOTA for PET/CT Imaging of Renal Function
title: A PET tracer that watches kidneys clear in real time
blurb: Al18F-NOTA clears through the kidneys fast in healthy mice and picks up real differences across three separate acute kidney injury models on PET. They've already taken it into a preliminary clinical study, further than most renal tracers get before someone writes them up.

original_title: Efficient Green Light‐Induced Photoclick Reactions Enabled by Triplet–Triplet Annihilation Photon Upconversion
title: Photoclick chemistry swaps UV for green light
blurb: Photoclick reactions usually need UV, which doesn't penetrate tissue and isn't kind to cells. Pairing the click chemistry with a triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion system, built around a palladium porphyrin sensitizer, lets green light drive the same reaction instead.

original_title: Aptamer-Based Heterobifunctional Targeted Degraders in Disease Treatment
title: Aptamers get recruited as the targeting half of protein degraders
blurb: A rundown of heterobifunctional degraders that swap the antibody half for an aptamer, leaning on aptamers' easy synthesis and programmability to drag disease proteins into the cell's own degradation machinery. Aimed at undruggable and resistant targets antibodies can't reach, but it's a survey of the field rather than one new result.

original_title: Picolinate- and Phosphonated Pyridyl-TACN Ligands for Highly Stable and Inert Cu(II) Complexes for Radiochemical Applications
title: New TACN ligands try to keep Cu(II) from wriggling loose
blurb: Picolinate and phosphonated-pyridine arms bolt onto a TACN scaffold to give copper(II) a snug five-coordinate cage, checked by titration, EPR, and cyclic voltammetry before it's put to work in 64Cu radiolabeling and PET imaging. Stability gets nailed down before any imaging claims are made.

original_title: Backbone-matched comparison of two trastuzumab-based antibody–drug conjugates: payload localization and gas-phase heterogeneity of trastuzumab deruxtecan and trastuzumab rezetecan
title: T-DXd and T-rezetecan look alike on paper, not in the mass spec
blurb: Same trastuzumab backbone, different payload chemistry, so the team ran HIC, native SEC-MS, and denaturing RPLC-MS side by side to map where each payload sits and how heterogeneous the two conjugates actually are in the gas phase. ADCs are never one molecule, they're a distribution, and this is what the two distributions look like next to each other.

original_title: Divergent Outcomes in Resilin-Like Peptide Cross-linking: Unexpected Photocatalytic Damage vs Enzymatic Success.
title: Enzymes cross-link resilin peptides cleanly, light doesn't
blurb: Photocatalytic cross-linking of resilin-like peptides causes damage that the enzymatic route avoids, so for this particular material light isn't the shortcut it usually is.

original_title: NANOCORPOS ANTI-HER2 CONJUGADOS A FÁRMACOS: AVANÇOS EM SISTEMAS DE LIBERAÇÃO PARA TUMORES SÓLIDOS E SNC
title: Anti-HER2 nanobody conjugates make a play for the brain
blurb: A literature review on anti-HER2 nanobody-drug conjugates as a smaller stand-in for full antibodies, sized to get around the tumor penetration and CNS access problems monoclonal ADCs run into. It's a survey, not new data, but the CNS angle is the part worth tracking.

original_title: Terminal Modification Reprograms Supramolecular Organization of Integrin Ligand Assemblies to Shape Cell Migration
title: Same peptide, different end cap, completely different cell behavior
blurb: Just modifying the N- or C-terminus of the integrin ligand FFFIKVAV, sequence untouched, reshuffles how it self-assembles, and that alone changes integrin activation and cell migration. A cheap knob to turn compared to redesigning the whole ligand.

original_title: A γ-AApeptide-Based Antibody-like Peptidomimetic for Enhanced EGFR-Targeted PET Imaging
title: A peptide mimic that punches like an antibody for EGFR PET
blurb: Dimerizing a γ-AApeptide EGFR-binding ligand into a cyclic antibody-like scaffold takes affinity from 0.67 μM down to 0.11 μM, a sixfold jump over the monomer, before it heads into PET imaging. Chasing antibody-level binding without an actual antibody.

original_title: Copper-Catalyzed Strain-Driven Enantiospecific C–C Oxidative Addition
title: Copper finally does the C-C bond trick palladium usually gets paid for
blurb: Copper hasn't managed oxidative addition into a C-C bond before. Here it cracks gem-difluorocyclopropanes enantiospecifically with anilines to give branched fluoroallylamines, and the combined experimental and computational work backs an actual C-C oxidative addition at copper, plus an unusual concerted substitution step along the way. A new elementary step for copper catalysis, not just a new product.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Development and Validation of an Analytical Method for the Assay of Deucravacitinib Tablet Formulation by HPLC
title: An HPLC method to keep deucravacitinib tablets honest
blurb: A validated HPLC assay for deucravacitinib tablets, ammonium acetate/ACN mobile phase, 240 nm detection, retention time 3.699 min, precision 0.45%. Unglamorous but exactly the kind of QC method a generic manufacturer actually needs.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Simultaneous Quantification of Ketamine and Its Metabolites in Rat Plasma Using LC-MS/MS: Method Development, Validation, and Application
title: Watching ketamine turn into its metabolites in rat plasma
blurb: An LC-MS/MS method that measures ketamine alongside norketamine and hydroxynorketamine in the same run, using a simple protein-precipitation prep. Parent-drug-only measurements apparently don't tell you enough about disposition, hence the metabolite tracking.

original_title: Ligand design broadens NiI-catalysed C(sp2)–heteroatom couplings of aryl bromides at low catalyst loadings
title: Getting Ni(I) coupling down to 100 ppm catalyst
blurb: NiI/NiIII C(sp2)-heteroatom coupling has been stuck with sluggish oxidative addition and fat catalyst loadings. A ligand/additive design that balances NiI reactivity against stability fixes both, pushing aryl bromide couplings with nucleophiles down to 100 ppm Ni. That's palladium-loading territory for a nickel system.

original_title: Atroposelective Pd(0)‐Catalyzed Direct Intermolecular C─H Arylation of Thiazole N ‐Oxides Provides Access to Heterobiaryls
title: Building chiral heterobiaryls straight off a C-H bond
blurb: Pd(0)-catalyzed direct arylation at C4 of thiazole N-oxides forges the atropochiral axis in one step, no prefunctionalized coupling partner needed. A designer chiral monodentate phosphine gets high enantioselectivity across a broad substrate set, including two different heteroaryl partners.

original_title: Combined radioligand therapy and immunotherapy for cancer: research advances and translational challenges.
title: Pairing radioligand therapy with immunotherapy
blurb: A review on combining radioligand therapy with immunotherapy for cancer and the translational obstacles still in the way. Light on specifics beyond that framing.

original_title: Architecture-Guided Sequential Editing of Distinct Disulfides in Unprotected Peptides
title: Editing one disulfide in a peptide without touching its neighbors
blurb: Aromatic, ethyl, and tert-butyl disulfides sitting in the same unprotected peptide turn out to have distinct intrinsic reactivities, so matched activation modes can address them one at a time and in sequence, no protecting groups required. Aromatic disulfides get an extra trick: an orthogonal phosphite-mediated transformation on top.

original_title: Cross-section measurement of 165Ho(d,x) reactions and comparison of deuteron and proton activation of holmium for165Er production
title: Deuterons vs protons for making Er-165
blurb: Cross-section measurements for 165Ho(d,x) reactions, set against the proton-activation route, sizing up the two paths to producing 165Er.

original_title: Discovery of (177)Lu-PSMA-MN4 as an improved PSMA-targeted radioligand with enhanced antitumor efficacy.
title: A PSMA radioligand upgrade in Lu-177-PSMA-MN4
blurb: A newly discovered PSMA-targeted radioligand, Lu-177-PSMA-MN4, reported to give better antitumor efficacy than what's out there. No comparator numbers to go on yet, just the claim.

original_title: NorthStar Secures Up to $185 Million Growth Financing Led by Hercules Capital to Scale Actinium-225 Production and Radiopharmaceutical Manufacturing for Next-Generation Precision Cancer Therapies - Business Wire
title: NorthStar banks up to $185M to scale up actinium-225
blurb: Hercules Capital leads a growth financing round for NorthStar to expand Ac-225 production and radiopharmaceutical manufacturing. It's a funding round, not a production milestone, so the actual output increase is still to be seen.

original_title: Asymmetric Divergent Synthesis of Miophytocen D, Roridin E, Verrucarin J, and Verrucarol
title: One divergent synthesis, four trichothecene natural products
blurb: A single asymmetric route to miophytocen D, roridin E, verrucarin J, and verrucarol, built on an exo-selective Diels-Alder, a biomimetic oxacyclization, a conformation-controlled alkene-epoxide cyclization, and an RCM macrocyclization. It delivers the first total synthesis of miophytocen D and hundred-milligram-scale verrucarol, plus evidence bearing on the proposed biosynthesis.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Highly Stereoselective Reaction of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes and Isatins
title: Getting a reluctant ketone to react with a strained ring
blurb: Isatins' ketone carbonyl is a lousy electrophile and sterically crowded, which is why Lewis-acid additions of bicyclobutanes to ketones haven't worked before. La(OTf)3 fixes that, delivering cyclobutenyl-hydroxyoxindoles in up to 97% yield and >20:1 dr, with control experiments and DFT backing up why.

original_title: Axial Ligand Tuning of the Catalytic Two- versus Four-Electron Reduction of Dioxygen by a Dinuclear Cobalt Complex
title: Tuning a cobalt catalyst's taste for oxygen with a spare ligand
blurb: Swap the axial ligand on a flexible dicobalt complex and you shift whether O2 reduction stops at peroxide or runs all the way to water. Bare in acetonitrile it gives a mixed 2e-/4e- outcome; add something like triphenylphosphine and the selectivity moves. A rare case where you can point to the molecular knob doing the switching.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Tracing Covalent Organic Framework Assembly through Kinetic Deceleration
title: Slowing a COF reaction down enough to catch it mid-build
blurb: COF assembly mechanisms have mostly been assumed, not shown. By deliberately decelerating a normally fast Schiff-base condensation, they grew millimeter-sized single crystals of the actual reaction intermediate and solved its structure, catching the framework forming instead of just inferring it afterward.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Cobalt‐Catalyzed Desymmetrizing Hydrogenation of Cyclic Anhydrides
title: A 3d metal crashes cyclic anhydride desymmetrization
blurb: Cobalt-catalyzed desymmetrizing hydrogenation turns cyclic 1,2- and 1,3-diacid anhydrides into chiral gamma- and delta-lactones, broad substrate scope, up to 99% ee, and it scales to grams. Worth noting mainly because this flavor of asymmetric hydrogenation is usually precious-metal turf.

original_title: Aluminum Cation-Catalyzed C2–H Activation and Enantioselective Michael Addition of Indoles
title: An aluminum cation doing a transition metal's C-H activation job
blurb: Prolinol-supported aluminum cations activate the C2-H bond of 3-substituted indoles and drive an enantioselective Michael addition to enones, good to excellent ee. The actual selling point: unlike the transition-metal versions, it doesn't need specially chelating enones to work.

original_title: Synthesis of Functionalized Cyanamide Derivatives Enabled by Hydrocyanamidation of Activated Alkenes or Alkynes
title: Cyanamides from alkenes without a metal in sight
blurb: Fluoride-promoted, metal-free hydrocyanamidation pairs NCTS with activated alkenes or alkynes to give disubstituted cyanamides, broad scope and good functional group tolerance, and it holds up on gram scale with late-stage functionalization to show for it.

original_title: Analysis of the off-target interaction of amyloid PET tracers with human brain sulfotransferases.
title: Amyloid PET tracers might be binding more than amyloid
blurb: A look at whether amyloid PET tracers cross-react with human brain sulfotransferases, off-target binding that would be worth knowing about before trusting the scan is reading amyloid alone.

original_title: Using a radiopharmaceutical production cyclotron for radiobiological research
title: Turning a radioisotope cyclotron into a proton therapy testbed
blurb: Bern is repurposing its 18 MeV medical cyclotron, built for radioisotope production, into a preclinical proton therapy research platform, opening it up to things like FLASH and spatially fractionated radiotherapy without building a dedicated beamline for it.

original_title: Streamlined Access to Steroid‐Like Frameworks With Vicinal Tertiary and Quaternary Centers via Pd‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Bisallylation
title: Building steroid-like scaffolds two stereocenters at a time
blurb: A Pd-catalyzed asymmetric bisallylation/ring-closing metathesis cascade assembles polycyclic frameworks with adjacent tertiary and all-carbon quaternary stereocenters straight from coumarin-derived starting material, a vicinal stereodyad pairing that's been notoriously hard to set catalytically.

original_title: Dual-Tracer (68)Ga-PSMA and (68)Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT in Advanced Prostate Cancer: Persistent PSMA Expression Despite Clinically Suspected Treatment-Emergent Neuroendocrine Differentiation.
title: PSMA sticks around even when the tumor looks like it's switching identity
blurb: A dual-tracer Ga-68 PSMA/DOTATATE PET/CT case in advanced prostate cancer where PSMA expression persisted despite clinical suspicion of treatment-emergent neuroendocrine differentiation, a reminder not to assume the tumor has fully switched lineage just because the picture looks that way.

original_title: Rapid Deprotection of O - and N -Benzyl Groups by Catalytic Transfer Hydrogenation with Industrially Viable Silane Reagents
title: Debenzylation without the hydrogen tank
blurb: Wet Pd/C plus a hydride donor, TMDS or PMHS, swaps in for H2 gas to strip O- and N-benzyl groups, mild and fast enough to read like a real process fix rather than a bench curiosity. No high-pressure hydrogenation rig needed, which is presumably the whole point if you're trying to run this in a plant.

original_title: Overriding Intrinsic Regioselectivity in Propargylic Substitution via Cu/Pd Synergistic Catalysis for Enantioselective Dienylation
title: Steering propargylic chemistry to the middle carbon instead
blurb: Cu/Pd working together forces nucleophilic attack onto the central carbon of a propargyl/allenyl-metal intermediate, a site this reaction normally ignores, to build 1,3-dienes with better than 20:1 regioselectivity, up to 99% ee, and clean E/Z control. DFT backs up why the two metals split the job the way they do.

original_title: Chiral Arylthiol-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrodifluoroalkylation of Alkenes Facilitated by Noncovalent Interaction
title: A chiral thiol talks a difluoroalkylation into picking sides
blurb: Photocatalysis with a C2-symmetric arylthiol adds alpha-bromodifluoroamides across methyleneindanes to give chiral gem-difluorinated indane amides in good yield and high ee. The real trick is a gem-dimethyl group on the substrate that widens the energy gap between the competing diastereomeric pathways, not the catalyst doing it alone.

original_title: When Reactions Cross Back: Dynamical Effects in Manganese–Oxo Epoxidation
title: Two nearly identical ligands, two different epoxidation outcomes
blurb: Swap pyridine for 4-tert-butylpyridine on a manganese-oxo epoxidation catalyst, barely a change on paper, and the reactivity and stereoselectivity shift anyway. The explanation isn't the usual electronic or steric ligand story but a dynamical one: trajectories crossing back over the barrier instead of just settling where the transition-state energy says they should.

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed Directed Asymmetric C–H Arylation Leading to a P-Stereogenic Center
title: An -OH group directs its way to a P-stereogenic center
blurb: A phenolic OH paired with an oxopiperidine carboxylic acid ligand directs Pd-catalyzed C(sp2)-H arylation right onto phosphorus, delivering P-stereogenic products in up to 90% yield and 98% ee across 30 substrates. Directed C-H activation doing stereocenter-setting work that usually needs a dedicated chiral auxiliary.

original_title: Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Alkylation of Aldimines with Unactivated Alkyl Iodides
title: Nickel radical chemistry that skips the activated alkyl halides
blurb: Reductive alkylation of N-sulfonyl and N-aryl aldimines runs at room temperature with plain primary, secondary, and even tertiary alkyl iodides, no directing group required. Mechanistic work points to a free alkyl radical adding outer-sphere, backed up with a gram-scale run and some beta-amino ester derivatization.

original_title: Convergent Synthesis of a Desmethyl Analogue of Amycomycin
title: Amycomycin's desmethyl cousin, the hard way
blurb: The first convergent route to a desmethyl amycomycin analogue died on an aldol condensation that steric hindrance killed on the real substrate, so they rebuilt around nucleophilic vinyl addition and a Boron-Wittig to get the congested vinyl boronate, plus a late-stage O-to-C acyl transfer to close out the tetramic acid core. More a story of a route failing and getting fixed than a clean one-shot synthesis.

original_title: Deboronative Asymmetric Suzuki–Miyaura Cross-Coupling of Alkylboronic Esters Enabled by Dual Photoredox and Nickel Catalysis
title: Racemic alkylboronic esters, sorted out by light and nickel together
blurb: First enantioconvergent Suzuki coupling to take racemic alkylboronic esters and (hetero)aryl bromides to a single enantiomer, using photoredox and nickel side by side. It needs both 4-cyanopyridine and pentafluoropyridine in the mix to get reactivity and selectivity together, so the ligand pairing is doing real work, not just filling out the SI.

original_title: Electrophile-Dependent Chemo- and Regioselectivity in Cu/Pd-Catalyzed Allylboration of Enynes
title: Same enyne, two different products, just change the leaving group
blurb: Cu/Pd-catalyzed allylboration of 1,3-enynes goes one way or the other depending only on the carbonate electrophile: allyl carbonates give borylated 1,4-enallenes, dienyl carbonates redirect the same system toward propargylation instead. The electrophile is picking the pathway here, not the catalyst.

original_title: Integrated Development and Manufacturing for Complex Bioconjugation - Fierce Pharma
title: Bioconjugation development and manufacturing, under one roof
blurb: A Fierce Pharma note on consolidating bioconjugate development and manufacturing into one integrated operation rather than splitting the work across vendors. Reads like an industry positioning piece more than news of an actual product or deal.

original_title: Rh(III)‐Catalyzed Cascade C─H Activation/[4 + 1] Annulation: A Direct Route to Benzofuran‐Fused Succinimides From Aromatic Acids and 3‐Methylmaleimides
title: Rh(III) stitches aromatic acids and maleimides into benzofuran-succinimides
blurb: A [4+1] annulation where Rh(III) first isomerizes 3-methylmaleimide into an exo-methylidene intermediate, then C-H activates the aromatic acid to build a rhodacycle before the two halves fuse into a benzofuran-fused succinimide. Also handles the bulkier 3,4-dimethylmaleimides, so the mechanism isn't just papering over one narrow substrate.

original_title: Visible-Light-Mediated Skeletal Editing of Furans to Pyridazines
title: Swap a furan's oxygen for a diazine, using just light and hydrazine
blurb: Visible-light photocatalysis trades a furan's oxygen for an N-N pair from hydrazine hydrate, turning furans into di-, tri-, and tetrasubstituted pyridazines with full regiocontrol, metal-free, at room temperature, in air. Works at gram scale and on late-stage complex molecules, and the mechanistic catch is that water keeps hydrazine from simply quenching the photocatalyst.

original_title: Electrochemically Supported Asymmetric Synthesis on Chiral Encoded Pt and Pt–Ir Surfaces
title: Teaching a platinum electrode to be chiral, no ligand required
blurb: A conspectus on building chirality straight into Pt and Pt-Ir electrode surfaces, using liquid-crystal templating and molecular imprinting during electrodeposition to leave behind mesoporous, chiral recognition sites. The stereochemistry lives in the metal, so the enantioselective step needs no chiral ligand at all.

original_title: Engineering In/In2O3 Heterointerfaces for Highly Efficient Acidic CO2-to-HCOOH Electroreduction at Ampere-Level Current Density
title: Zapping a CO2-to-formic-acid catalyst back to life between pulses
blurb: In2O3 is good at steering acidic CO2 reduction toward formic acid, but its In3+ sites keep getting reduced to dead metallic indium. Here, periodic anodic pulses on an In/In2O3 interface reoxidize the catalyst on the fly, holding ampere-level current density that steady-state operation just can't sustain.

original_title: Intermolecular [2 + 2] Cycloaddition of Oxime Ethers with Indole Derivatives via Visible Light Energy Transfer Catalysis
title: Energy-transfer catalysis snaps oxime ethers onto indoles
blurb: A visible-light energy-transfer-catalyzed [2+2] between indoles and oxime ethers builds fused or bridged rings carrying both indole and azetidine units in one step. A fairly direct route into a scaffold that's otherwise a pain to assemble.

original_title: Computational Insights into Mn and Fe Azoaromatic Pincer Complexes: Modulating Ligands for Enhanced CO2-to-Formic Acid Conversion
title: DFT picks out iron pincer catalysts that might ditch the base for CO2-to-formic-acid
blurb: A computational screen of eight Mn(I) and Fe(II) azoaromatic pincer complexes for hydrogenating CO2 to formic acid without strong base, in water. Two iron ligands, L1 and L2, come back with computed turnover frequencies north of a million per hour at room temperature. All numbers so far are DFT, nobody's made the winning catalyst yet.

original_title: From α,β-Unsaturated Amide to Enamide: Intramolecular Alkene Translocation via Iridium-Catalyzed Transfer Hydrogenation
title: Moving a double bond across an amide without touching the amide
blurb: An Ir-catalyzed transfer hydrogenation walks the alkene in an unsaturated amide clean across the linkage into an enamide, flipping it from electrophilic to nucleophilic. Redox-neutral, no strong base needed, and it runs through an irreversible intramolecular hydrogen transfer. They've also got early results doing it enantioselectively.

original_title: Enantioselective Strain-Release Formal (3 + 3) Cycloaddition of 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes to Chiral 1,4-Diazabicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Relay Dy/Ir Catalysis
title: Relay Dy/Ir catalysis turns strained azabicyclobutanes into rigid chiral piperazine mimics
blurb: The first catalytic enantioselective (3+3) cycloaddition of azabicyclobutanes, with Dy(OTf)3 cracking the strained ring open and Ir handling the stereochemistry in relay. The payoff is a rigid, sp3-rich diazabicycloheptane scaffold, giving pyrazine and piperazine chemistry a defined 3D shape they never had alongside the rigidity.

original_title: Diboron‐Enabled Nickel‐Catalyzed Intermolecular Reductive Coupling of Styrenes With Aldehydes
title: Ni catalysis couples styrenes straight to aldehydes, no organometallic needed
blurb: A diboron/MeOLi combo lets nickel run reductive coupling of styrenes with aliphatic aldehydes intermolecularly, skipping the preformed organometallic reagents this kind of carbonyl addition usually demands. Up to 93% yield with high linear selectivity, and deuterium labeling backs the mechanism.

original_title: Catalytic Alkene Hydrosilylation and Dinitrogen Silylation by Bis(silylene) and Bis(diphenylphosphino) Cobalt Chlorides
title: Swap silylene for phosphine on the same cobalt pincer, get a different C-H story
blurb: Same dipyrromethene backbone, two different donor sets: the silylene [SiC(sp3)Si] pincer oxidatively adds into its own bridging methylene C-H bond to give a Co(III) hydride, while the phosphine [PC(sp3)P] analog doesn't. That divergence feeds straight into which ligand set actually wins at catalyzing olefin hydrosilylation and dinitrogen silylation.

original_title: Association of Zinc Supplementation with Recombinant Protein Recovery and Crystallization
title: A zinc-dependent protease needed more zinc than the protocol gave it
blurb: Batch-to-batch yields for a Zn2+-dependent metalloprotease from C. acnes kept drifting even with identical purification steps, and standard optimization couldn't fix it. AlphaFold2 modeling against a Zn2+-bound homolog pointed to an under-occupied metal site, and supplementing zinc restored consistent recovery and crystallization. Not a flashy fix, but one that buffer-tweaking alone would never have found.

original_title: Contact-electro-catalyzed direct hydroxylation of aromatic C–H bonds under ambient conditions
title: Phenols from C–H bonds, no UV lamp needed
blurb: Aromatic C–H hydroxylation normally needs UV light or a pile of sacrificial oxidant to make hydroxyl radicals. Here contact electrification at a PTFE-water interface generates both ·OH and a strong interfacial field to do the job at room temperature, no lamp involved.

original_title: Anion Engineering of Surface Frustrated Lewis Pairs for Light‐Assisted CO 2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
title: Tuning the base half of a frustrated Lewis pair for once
blurb: Most surface frustrated-Lewis-pair catalysts get tuned on the Lewis-acid, metal side; this one nitrides zinc gallium oxide instead, doping in nitrogen to reshape the anion coordination, generate oxygen vacancies, and rework the Lewis-basic sites. Built for light-assisted CO2 hydrogenation to methanol, with the acid side left untouched.

original_title: Synthesis of α-Chlorocarbonyls through Kharasch-Type Addition and Cotelomerization Driven by Photoredox/Cobalt Dual Catalysis
title: One-pot alkyl-chloride installation across Michael acceptors
blurb: A photoredox/cobalt dual-catalyst system runs Kharasch-type addition and cotelomerization together: an alkyl radical adds to a Michael acceptor, then cobalt chloride delivers chlorine to the resulting α-carbonyl radical. Net result is alkyl and chloride landing on the same molecule in one step from ordinary alkyl radical precursors and a collidine·HCl salt, and it reportedly tolerates several different ways of generating that starting radical.

original_title: Synergistic Linkage Engineering in Donor–Acceptor Covalent Organic Frameworks for NIR-II Absorption and Efficient Photothermal Conversion
title: Covalent organic frameworks tuned to absorb further into the infrared
blurb: Combining linkage engineering with donor-acceptor design to push a covalent organic framework's absorption into the NIR-II window and control how the excited state decays. The point is getting a COF to do NIR-II light-to-heat conversion at all, since that pairing has been the hard part.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Engineering an Artificial Metalloenzyme for Efficient Photo‐Enzymatic CO 2 Conversion
title: Bolting a rhodium catalyst directly onto formate dehydrogenase
blurb: Photo-enzymatic CO2 reduction usually loses efficiency because the photocatalyst and enzyme sit apart and electron transfer lags. This covalently tethers a tailored rhodium complex, the best of nine screened, to formate dehydrogenase, so light-driven NADH regeneration and CO2 conversion happen on one hybrid catalyst instead of shuttling between two.

original_title: PEG-Heparin hydrogels allow for the assessment of breast cancer tumouroid response to anti-cancer treatment for personalised medicine
title: 3D hydrogel breast tumor models built for patient-derived tumouroids, not just cell lines
blurb: A bioengineered PEG-heparin hydrogel meant to track how breast cancer cell lines, and more usefully patient-derived tumouroids, respond to treatment in 3D. They start by checking with UV spectroscopy that the drug and hydrogel don't interfere with each other, basic groundwork but necessary before trusting any dose-response reading out of the gel.

original_title: Unexpected Rearrangement of Unsaturated Lactones to Give Tricyclic Furopyrrolidinones
title: Cyanide doesn't just add once, it rearranges the whole lactone
blurb: Feeding α,β,γ,δ-unsaturated lactones with the right aryl substituents cyanide gets multiple additions instead of one, rearranging the scaffold into tricyclic furopyrrolidinones that stitch together ether, nitrile, and lactam groups. The outcome depends on stoichiometry and substrate, and X-ray structures back a dynamic equilibrium behind it rather than a one-way path.

original_title: Single-Atom Nickel-Catalyzed C–H Amidation of Pyridine and Quinoline N-Oxides
title: A single-atom nickel catalyst that skips straight from quinoline to amidated N-oxides
blurb: A Ni-N4 single-atom catalyst, confirmed by EXAFS, does direct C–H amidation of quinoline and pyridine N-oxides with dioxazolones, giving a broad set of 2-acetamidoquinoline N-oxides. Two one-pot routes starting from plain quinoline get you there, or on to the pharmaceutically relevant 2-aminoquinolines, and the catalyst holds up to recycling.

original_title: Nanopore Engineering in Scalable Metal–Organic Frameworks for C2H4 Purification from Ternary Mixtures
title: MOF pores tuned to pull ethylene cleanly out of a three-gas mixture
blurb: Separating C2H4 from CO2 and C2H2 is a pain since all three are close in size and polarity. Two new pcu-type MOFs, Zn-Atz-Msa and Zn-Mtz-Msa, tweak the functional groups on triazole ligands and add a flexible methylsuccinic acid linker to dial in the pore environment, aimed at pulling clean ethylene straight out of the ternary mix.
